06-product-planning.notes: Planning task: there were no tests to run. Grading came from reading every RESPONSE.md and the key sections of every PLAN.md (assumptions, conflict policy, purge/24h, milestones, decisions), backed by grep checks for fake dates and staffing and for topic coverage. All 28 submissions supply PLAN.md and RESPONSE.md with three assumptions, and BRIEF/TASK are unchanged. The main differentiator was whether the 24h-after-acceptance rule survives a tablet that is offline when acceptance happens. Strong answers purge at confirmed submission (D, G, N, O, V), gate acceptance on purge or checkout (E, K, P, AA), or layer a server-anchored cap with an interlock (AB, C). Weaker answers purge only once the tablet observes acceptance (T, W, X, Z, Y, B) or key the purge to sync (A). Close calls: N vs D (N has a fuller decision register; D is tighter and lists the longest chain); P vs K (same acceptance-barrier approach; K's risk reasoning is deepest but its prose and proportionality are weaker); E vs I (E's purge design is better, I's product UX is better). Fake dates and staffing were penalised in A, B and Y, with lighter penalties for invented numbers in V, S and U. V's chat-without-tools process note did not affect the score because nothing needed to run. Not verified: whether any submission's API sketches are internally implementable beyond reading.

10-general-operations.notes: Ranking: Z, N and AB are top-tier. N and Z tie on 9.5; Z goes first for the 'latest safe points' patch analysis and contradictions nobody else raised (does the patch touch the demo environment, Thursday carrying two hard items). Below them, I, J and Q (9.0-8.75) all have the right chains; they lose points for invented dates (I), fallback slots that clash or break the uninterrupted rule (J), and an unscheduled change window (Q). Common failures across submissions: deploying Friday when QA could run Tuesday (C, D, H, P, T, U, Y and others), skipping Tuesday for QA (D, L, P, T, AA), finance fallbacks that are not two uninterrupted hours (H 1.5h, R/W/AA using the split Wednesday morning), and S deferring the review to Thursday. Almost everyone spotted the core trap, that Wednesday 15:00 falls inside the unavailable block, and moved the demo to Thursday 16:00. They were separated by how well they handled the second-order ambiguities (whether the user must attend, whether Sam must join the demo, whether the Tuesday leadership meeting is the recurring one, whose finance hours, the exact SLA times). G was produced in a chat with no tools, per its process note; that has no effect on this prose task beyond what is graded. 12-frontend-editorial.notes: All 28 load with no remote requests and no horizontal overflow at 1440/390. Every one has a working reading-mode control and inline email validation, so scores split on taste, layout defects and accessibility details. Close calls: G edges AB, D and X on how well its waterline motif is integrated and its accessibility (sr-only h1 context, radios plus size toggle, all contrast passing). AB, D and X tie at 9.25. T and U share a near-identical design language; they scored the same. Reveal-on-scroll pages (B, E, I, R) look blank in the full-page captures, but scrolling the page in Playwright made every hidden element visible. Contrast was computed with a DOM text-node walker (alpha-composited backgrounds), not axe. Fills using background-clip (AA 'Low', X 'Water') register 1.00 and were treated as false positives. E's unreadable toggle state appears only under hover. Tie-breaks: 9.25 AB > D > X (richness); 8.5 L > AA > T > U; 8.25 Z > B > Y; 5.75 W > Q > C (C's success card shows on page load, a functional bug).
